title: Working length & apical size: the evidence
topic: What outcome studies say about stopping 0–2 mm short of the radiographic apex and about apical size, and how weak the evidence is.

claims.claim: Toy model / schematic: apex sketch labeled radiographic apex, major foramen (opening on the side, off the root tip), minor constriction, CDJ; 'schematic / not to scale'
claims.source: Textbook apical anatomy (Hargreaves & Berman, Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp; not re-read). No number shown. Off-tip foramen is consistent with Martos et al., Int Endod J 2009;42:329-34 (PMID 19220517; abstract: foramen at the root tip in 40%). A constriction is often absent (Wu et al., OOOOE 2000;89:99-103, PMID 10630950; abstract)

claims.claim: Green zone 0–2 mm short of the radiographic apex; slips 94% '0–2 mm short' · 76% 'long' (red scribble drawn out of the foramen and past the dashed 0 line = beyond the radiographic apex) · 68% '>2 mm short' — 'healed · necrotic + lesion · 8–10 yr'
claims.source: Sjögren et al., J Endod 1990;16:498-504 (PMID 2084204). PubMed abstract gives design (356 patients, 8-10 yr) and that the level of the root filling significantly affected outcome; the 94/76/68 breakdown is full-text data confirmed only through secondary quotation (PMC3574741), primary full text not read: check against the paper's results table before posting. Unit = roots; one Swedish cohort

Two cohorts with different metrics, hence 'worse'. Chugal et al., Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol Oral Radiol Endod 2003;96:81-90 (PMID 12847449; abstract: in teeth with apical periodontitis each mm of working length lost raised the chance of failure by 14%; measured from the radiographic apex; 4 yr). Ng et al., Int Endod J 2011;44:583-609 (PMID 21366626; full text read by the fact-checker, not in the abstract: OR 0.88, 95% CI 0.79-0.97, i.e. 12% lower odds of success per un-instrumented mm short of the apex-locator zero; primary and retreatment roots, 2-4 yr)

claims.claim: <#30 vs ≥#30: 'irrigant reaches apical third (in vitro)'; 'debris' left in the smaller preparation
claims.source: Khademi et al., J Endod 2006;32:417-20 (PMID 16631839; abstract: SEM of debris/smear layer in 40 mesiobuccal canals of extracted mandibular first molars, syringe irrigation; minimum size #30 for irrigant penetration to the apical third). Toy model / schematic: the flow lines and specks are drawn, not simulated; consistent with Boutsioukis & Gutierrez Nova, J Endod 2021;47:1487-95 (PMID 34118256; abstract; computational model). Depends on taper and needle size

claims.claim: RCT · healed at 12 mo: binding file +2 → 48%; +3 or more → 71–92%
claims.source: Saini et al., J Endod 2012;38:1309-15 (PMID 22980168; abstract: 48%, 71.43%, 80%, 84.61%, 92% for 2-6 sizes past the first apical binding file; mandibular first molars; 129 evaluated at 12 months; only +2 significantly worse, +3 to +6 not different from each other)

claims.claim: Summary 1: Infected: fill 0–2 mm short of x-ray apex
claims.source: Sjögren 1990 (PMID 2084204) as above: level of the root filling relative to the radiographic apex. Limited to infected roots because in Chugal 2003 (PMID 12847449; abstract) teeth with a normal pulp and periapex showed the reverse: successes ended 1.23 mm and failures 0.20 mm short of the radiographic apex

Saini 2012 (PMID 22980168) as above. In Fatima et al., J Endod 2021;47:1345-51 (PMID 34058250; abstract), +2 sizes with a 4% taper had the lowest success (57.1%); +2 with a 6% taper did not differ from +3. The first binding file is a poor gauge of apical diameter (Wu et al., Int Endod J 2002;35:264-7, PMID 11985678; abstract)

claims.claim: Evidence: LOW · cohorts · in vitro · small RCTs
claims.source: Descriptive tag. A published 'low' rating exists for apical size and healing only: Sabeti et al., J Endod 2024;50:292-8 (PMID 38135112; abstract: 2 studies, overall quality of evidence low). The working-length data are observational cohorts and were not formally graded

caption:
Where to stop, and how big? The evidence on one board.

WHERE: necrotic pulp + lesion, per root, 8–10 yr, one cohort: 94% healed when filled 0–2 mm short of the radiographic apex, 76% long, 68% >2 mm short. Two more cohorts: about 12–14% worse odds per mm short. Vital teeth showed the reverse trend.

HOW BIG: in vitro, irrigant reached the apical third from ~#30. An RCT (mandibular molars, 12 mo): binding file +2 healed 48%, +3 to +6 71–92%; only +2 was significantly worse.

Evidence: low. Schematic animation.

Refs: Sjögren 1990, Khademi 2006, Saini 2012, Sabeti 2024 (J Endod); Chugal 2003 (OOOOE); Ng 2011 (Int Endod J).
